overall_summary: Deduplication reveals 47 unique videos showing a dramatic performance divide. First-person experiential what-if space/survival scenarios ('What If You Fell Into...') and striking cosmic paradoxes drive the highest view velocity (800–1,000+ views in under 7 days, peaking with Venus at 947 views in under 24 hours). In contrast, generic psychology snippets ('fake memories', 'earworms') and recycled basic space facts consistently flatline under 100 views.

winning_patterns.pattern: First-Person 'What If You Fell Into...' Survival Hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (825 views, 15 likes) dominate recent 7-day velocity and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Frame extreme cosmic phenomena as immersive first-person physical survival micro-journeys.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' generated 947 views and 21 likes within 16 hours of upload, outpacing older uploads rapidly.
winning_patterns.action: Lead immediately with a quantifiable physical contradiction in the first 1.5 seconds without preamble.

winning_patterns.evidence: Every top performer in the recent 7-day window (A9Qa-RmuOr0, IYuce8vaU3Y, YlDuGu1vzAg, 8KEl0_pJ_68) clocks between 19 and 21 seconds with higher like conversion.
winning_patterns.action: Structure narratives tightly for a 19–21 second runtime to maximize completion rate and loop potential.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5–53 views) and song-earworm facts (17–71 views) consistently failed to trigger algorithm distribution.
weak_patterns.action: Pause generic psychology facts unless anchored to an intense cinematic mystery or survival angle.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' posted 3 times plateaued at 33–220 views with negligible engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict deduplication; never repost identical core premises.
